requirements.requirement: curl held at its current version (8.12.1-4.el10) on node1 using a version-lock mechanism
requirements.summary: Baseline curl version captured (curl-8.12.1-4.el10), versionlock plugin installed, dnf versionlock add curl applied and confirmed listed as curl-0:8.12.1-4.el10.*

requirements.requirement: The hold survives a real system update (other packages update, curl remains untouched)
requirements.summary: A real dnf -y update ran and upgraded ~20 other packages (vim-minimal, tar, rsync, kernel-tools, rsyslog, qemu-guest-agent, etc. per rpm -qa --last); curl remained at 8.12.1-4.el10 throughout and dnf check-update curl showed no pending update afterward

requirements.requirement: Independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart boot identity/healthy state, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 21de1f79.../uptime 10:04:21 captured with curl and versionlock intact; reboot issued and acknowledged (stream closed, connection errors during downtime); node reconnected; post-restart boot_id 29da1d8e.../uptime 10:08:11 differs from baseline confirming an actual restart; curl version and versionlock entry unchanged after recovery. Cross-checked against fixed after-prepare (boot_id 21de1f79...) and after-executor (boot_id 29da1d8e...) snapshots, which are consistent with the executor's own before/after restart observations.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied: curl was locked at its installed version (8.12.1-4.el10) using dnf versionlock, and the lock was proven to survive a real dnf update that upgraded roughly 20 other packages while leaving curl untouched. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly, with distinct pre- and post-restart boot identities and recovered curl/versionlock state, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is good; the only residue is a trivial /tmp/reboot.log file from the required reboot action, and no unnecessary or unrelated mutations were found in the command trace.
limitations: The lifecycle snapshot's after_prepare phase is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled), so it cannot independently corroborate pre-executor state beyond what before_prepare shows; this does not affect the task since node1 is the only managed node and all comparisons are directly against before_prepare/after_executor.

Full stdout of the completed background dnf -y update (post cmd-aeb64412543744dc timeout) was not captured directly, though its completion and effects were confirmed indirectly via ps aux, rpm -qa --last, and post-update curl/versionlock checks.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command timeline reviewed chronologically: baseline checks, versionlock plugin install, versionlock add curl, an initial combined check-update+update command that hit a 120s proxy timeout (cmd-aeb64412543744dc) but whose underlying dnf -y update process continued running in the background (confirmed via ps aux) and completed successfully, upgrading ~20 packages while leaving curl untouched. This was not a discarded troubleshooting mutation — the update it kicked off directly produced the final verified evidence, so no separate unnecessary mutation occurred there. The reboot (cmd-f43fd07b5b6f4851) was a necessary state-changing action required for the independent restart-evidence protocol and was fully accounted for with pre/post verification. Minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log was created by the reboot command's output redirection and remained in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot; this is a trivial, low-risk artifact directly tied to the required restart action rather than an unrelated mutation, so it only lightly reduces the hygiene score. No failed services, no damaged package state (package-health checks show manager=dnf clean before and after), and no unsafe exposure changes — listening-socket differences before/after are only PID churn from the reboot, not new services.
